html:
The Venezuelan refugee crisis is the flight of millions of people from Venezuela since the mid 2010s. By the 2020s nearly eight million had left, the largest exodus ever recorded in the Americas.

Venezuela has some of the world's largest oil reserves, and in the 20th century it drew immigrants from Europe and its neighbours. Under Hugo Chávez (1999 to 2013) oil money paid for social programmes, but the economy came to depend on oil alone. After his death, Nicolás Maduro took over just as oil prices fell in 2014. The economy collapsed. Food and medicine ran short, hyperinflation wiped out wages, and the government jailed opponents and held disputed elections.

  • Colombia took in the most people, close to three million, and in 2021 gave them ten years of legal status.
  • Many others went to Peru, Brazil, Chile and Ecuador.
  • Later, many headed north through the dangerous Darién Gap toward the United States.

Many walked for weeks across the Andes. The crisis reshaped cities across South America and became a major issue in US immigration politics.
sum: The Venezuelan refugee crisis is the flight of millions of people from Venezuela since the mid 2010s. By the 2020s nearly eight million had left, the largest exodus ever recorded in the Americas.
